summary: In 14 trials, eating oily fish lowered triglycerides slightly (about 0.11 mmol/L on average) and raised HDL a little. This whole-food effect is much smaller than that of high-dose supplements.
whyThisGrade: Fish contains many nutrients, so the effect can't be put down to omega-3 alone

studies.title: Consumption of fish and vascular risk factors: A systematic review and meta-analysis of intervention studies
